purpose: Naproxen is used to relieve pain, reduce swelling, and lower fever. It helps with conditions like headaches, muscle aches, menstrual cramps, toothaches, backaches, and arthritis. It can also help with minor injuries like sprains.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling, and fever. Naproxen works by blocking the enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2) that produce these chemicals. With fewer prostaglandins being made, you feel less pain and swelling.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include upset stomach, heartburn, nausea, and stomach pain. Some people may experience headache, dizziness, or drowsiness. Taking it with food or milk can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: Naproxen can increase your risk of stomach bleeding, ulcers, heart attack, or stroke, especially if taken for a long time or in high doses. Avoid it if you have kidney problems, are pregnant (especially in the last 3 months), or are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Always talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining it with blood thinners or other pain relievers.
typical_dosing: For adults, the usual over-the-counter dose is 220 mg (one Aleve tablet) every 8 to 12 hours as needed. Do not take more than 660 mg in 24 hours unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Prescription doses may be higher and should be taken exactly as directed by your doctor.
